name: Residence Oliva
notes: From the street views (00, 01, 12: a slate-and-rust stone plinth wall with the garage let into it, a board-marked concrete volume on top with a long horizontal window band and a corten box framing its end, a taller black volume with a chimney behind, a concrete slab cantilevering east past it, a black wing to the west under a concrete roof slab that cantilevers well past its end, feather grasses on the bank) and the garden views (02, 05: one long low black house on the upper level, a deep timber-lined overhang on black posts over the terrace, a pool parallel to the house with a long shallow concrete beach at its east end and timber decking along both sides, solar panels on the roof in two groups tilted toward the garden, a wide lawn). This pass: the pool is a real pool set flush into the raised terrace (was a raised water box), its beach and decks let in flush; the solar panels drawn as three tilted rows plus a small group, glass over a pale metal frame so they read blue-grey with light gaps (were a single glass wedge tilted the wrong way); the concrete slab cantilevering east on the street side added; grasses on the street bank; the far garden tree made an umbrella crown. The site slopes down to the street, drawn as a raised grass terrace on the plinth; garden to the south, street to the north. The lengths of the wings, the plan depth and the pool's length are estimated from the wide garden photograph; the roofs themselves were not seen and are drawn dark. Refined 24 Sep 2026: the garden glazing given black mullions about every 3 m so it reads as the tall sliding panels of the garden photograph; the flat roofs (never photographed) drawn as gravel inside a dark or concrete rim rather than solid black, which had made the house read as one black slab from above - a guess; white sofas under the timber-lined overhang and dark sun loungers past the pool's beach, as in the garden views. Refined 21 Oct 2026 (three rounds against photos 00-12): the biggest mismatches were the pool, the garden's edge and the street planting. The pool in photos 02 and 05 is a long lap pool with a shallow sand-coloured beach at its far end and timber decking down both sides; it was 14 m and is now 22.5 m with 28 m decks, a 6.5 m beach and four dark loungers on it. The street front (photos 00, 01, 12) gains a stair of sleepers up the bank, three big dark-green shrubs with red tips on either side of the drive, and drifts of feather grass along the kerb. The lawn is closed on three sides by a perimeter hedge and a ring of mature trees, as in the wide garden photograph (05), and the west wing's garden glass takes one more mullion. Still guessed: the roofs (never photographed), the interior (photos 06-11), the extent of the slate plinth beyond the drive, the exact length of both wings.
